reasons.A: Long, evenly built explanatory sentences with 'First/Second/Third' scaffolding and a neutral manual tone; none of the passage's clipped rhythm or dry personal asides.
reasons.B: Closest rhythm: short declaratives mixed with occasional fuller sentences, plain uncontracted diction, dry understatement ('A dead one, of course'), fragments used about as often as the passage uses them.
reasons.C: Right register and plainness, but stacks fragments and one-line paragraphs more thickly than the passage ('Not just the gap.' 'No gaps.' 'That is all.'), tipping toward imitation.
